releaseNotes:
## 13.0.0

### Breaking changes
- `XamlSerializer` declares `CanRead` and `CanWrite`, and its `Serialize`/`Deserialize` overloads now implement `IDocumentSerializer` members. See the `Avalonia.Controls.Documents` changelog for the interface change.
- `XamlSerializer.SerializeAsync` and `DeserializeAsync` are removed; `Serialize` and `Deserialize` are the whole contract. The format does no asynchronous I/O - it is processor-bound and assembles its output in memory - so the async pair was a thread-pool hop that held a pool thread for the duration of synchronous work. Replace `await serializer.SerializeAsync(snapshot, stream, ct)` with `serializer.Serialize(snapshot, stream, ct)`, or `await Task.Run(() => serializer.Serialize(snapshot, stream, ct), ct)` to keep it off a UI thread; `FlowDocument.SaveAsync` and `LoadAsync` already do that wrapping.
- `XamlSerializer` takes `DocumentSerializerOptions`: `new XamlSerializer(options)`, matching `RtfSerializer` and `DocxSerializer`. It had only an implicit parameterless constructor, so `MaxImageBytes` could not reach it and the reader decoded a `RichImage` base64 payload of any size. An image over the cap is now dropped and the document around it still loads.

### Features
- `InlineFormatting.UnderlineStyle` round-trips as the `UnderlineStyle` attribute on an inline element. The writer previously emitted only `TextDecorations`, which records that an underline is on but not which of the ten line styles it is, so a `Dotted` or `Wave` underline came back as a plain one and every XAML save flattened what RTF and DOCX had preserved. All ten values round-trip, including `Wave` and `Word`, which no renderer draws faithfully. The attribute is written only for an explicit style: an unset (null) style writes nothing and reads back as null, keeping it distinct from an explicit `Single` so inherited formatting still merges as `child ?? parent`. An unrecognized spelling reads as `Single`, the style an unset value draws as.
- The document-wide footnote numbering round-trips as the `FootnoteNumberFormat` attribute on `<FlowDocument>`, written when not `Decimal`; the anchors render in it.
- Footnotes round-trip: the anchor as `<RichFootnoteReference NoteId="..."/>` (it carries no number, which is the position of its note among the notes) and note bodies as `<Footnote NoteId="...">` blocks inside a `<FlowDocument.Footnotes>` property element, written after the blocks and read wherever it appears. A note's `Label` attribute carries `Footnote.Label` when the note has one.
- Per-section page setup round-trips as `PageWidth`/`PageHeight`/`PagePadding` attributes on `<Section>`. The `<FlowDocument>` element now round-trips `PageWidth`/`PageHeight` too — previously only `PagePadding` survived, silently dropping a fixed page size.
- Page bands round-trip as a `<FlowDocument.PageBands>` property element of `<PageBand>` nested documents (written before the blocks) carrying `Role` and `Rule` attributes; a section's `Header`, `Footer`, `FirstPageHeader` and `FirstPageFooter` attributes reference bands by `Name`. The page-number field round-trips as `<RichPageNumberField Kind="..."/>`; it carries no number, which belongs to whoever paginates the document.
- Keep rules round-trip as block attributes: `KeepTogether`/`KeepWithNext` written when true, `WidowControl` written only when explicitly off (the default is on).
- Page breaks round-trip as the `BreakPageBefore="True"` attribute on the flagged block (the attribute was previously not serialized at all). A legacy `<RichPageBreak/>` element normalizes on read to the paragraph split + flag.

### Fixes
- A table's shape round-trips. Cell `ColumnSpan`/`RowSpan` were never written, so every merge collapsed to 1 on a XAML save and a row that carried one came back short with its columns shifted; a vertical merge's continuation cells exist only as the restart cell's `RowSpan`, so they vanished with it. The table's interior gridlines (`InsideBorderWidth`/`InsideBorderBrush`), a row's explicit height (`MinHeight`) and a cell's `VerticalAlignment` were dropped the same way, leaving a bordered table with an outer frame and no grid, rows collapsed to content height, and bottom- or centre-aligned cell text at the top.
- `TextElementFormatting.LetterSpacing` round-trips as the `LetterSpacing` attribute. It was written by no element and read by none, so character spacing a DOCX import had raised into the model - or the editor had set - was lost by every XAML save.
- An image, a page-number field or a footnote anchor nested inside a `RichSpan`, `RichBold`, `RichItalic`, `RichUnderline`, `RichSuperscript`, `RichSubscript` or `RichHyperlink` was dropped on read, so XAML did not read back what the writer emits. A linked picture came back as an empty hyperlink, a footnote anchor vanished while its note body survived as an orphan, and a "Page N" footer link came back empty. The two read paths are now one list of accepted elements.
